column2: The player-characters hear of a deity present in the city, perhaps manifesting at a temple. Roll [[1d20]]: on a result of 1-10, the rumor is unsubstantiated; on 11-20, the report comes from a reputable eyewitness.
A procession of honor, with a deity in attendance, travels down a major street or through an important plaza, etc.

A deity briefly manifests itself in an unexpected place. Roll [[1d20]]: on a result of 1-10, only the player-characters seem to know about it; on 11-19, there are guards, temple priests, etc., scurrying about; on 20, the deity strolls unattended through the crowded streets.

For a limited time, a deity will hear petitions at a temple. Roll [[1d20]]: on a result of 1-14, the player-characters can't get there in time or aren't admitted; on 15-20, they are admitted to the deity's presence. If they are admitted, roll [[1d20]] again: on a result of 1-12, the petition is turned down; on 13-19, the petition is granted; on 20, the deity grants a player-character a wish or kills him, depending on the nature of the petition.

The player-characters encounter a disguised deity who craves earthly amusement free of fawning worshipers. The deity may reward those player-characters who provide a good time and may be very hard on those who don't.
